描述_ZN: Booklet of "Western Mount Huashan Temple Tablet", 38 pages of topography, cut and framed, 3 lines per page, 6 characters per line. It is 22.3 cm in length and 12.8 cm in width.　　This stele was erected in the eighth year of Yanxi (165), in clerical script, elegant and magnificent. It is "the most powerful of the Han eighths, the first of the Wei steles" (Wang Xisun, Qing Dynasty). The name of the calligrapher is seldom left on Han inscriptions, but this inscription has the name of "Shuzo Xinfeng Guo Xiangcha Shu" at the end. The inscription describes the rituals of the emperors of successive dynasties and the restoration of the Huayue Temple by Yuan Feng, the governor of Hongnong in the current dynasty.　　The original stele Song Ouyang Xiu "collection of ancient records", Zhao Mingcheng "Jinshilu" recorded. According to Yuan Luo Tianchao's "Class Compilation Chang'an Zhi" and Ming Guo Zongchang's "Jin Shi Shi Shi", it is presumed that the monument was destroyed in the late Song and early Yuan dynasties. There are four trustworthy copies: one is the Chang Yuan version, named after the Ming Dynasty Chang Yuan Wang Wensun collection. The second is the Huayin book, which was collected by the Huayin East Shiu Shang brothers and Guo Zongchang in the Ming Dynasty, also known as the Guanzhong book. Third is the four Ming Ben, Ming Dynasty Ningbo Fengxi Wan scroll building and Fan Qin Tianyi Pavilion collection, Ningbo is known as the four Ming. Four is the Shunde book, because of the Qing season Shunde Li Wentian was stored and named.　　The Huayin version is finely topologized with thick ink. The first to seventeenth lines of the original stele have more than one hundred characters of dancing, which is later than the Chang Yuan and Shun De Ben, about between Song and Yuan. More than 230 inscriptions and comments by Guo Zongchang, Wang Duo, Weng Fanggang, Ruan Yuan, etc. are present on the accompanying pages. Among them, Wang Hong wrote a postscript: "advocate the Han clerical when and Changli text from the same work of the same eight generations"; Zhu Yun postscript from the theory of six books to examine the structure of the inscriptions, to prove the progression of seal, official, regular; Zhu Xigeng postscript detailing the flow of the Huashan stele all toppings passed to the collection, all have high academic value.　　It is also recorded in the books such as Song Hong Shih's "Official Interpretation" and Qing Ruan Yuan's "Han Yanxi Xiyue Huashan Temple Tablet Examination".
